titulo: Using ir in the imperfect to say was / were going to
subtitulo: Iba a llamarte: plans that were about to happen, or didn't.
regla: Ir in the imperfect (iba, ibas, iba, íbamos, iban) + a + infinitive = was / were going to: plans, things about to happen.

bloques.texto: To say _was / were going to_ do something, use **ir** in the **imperfect** + **a** + **infinitive**.
It's used for actions that **were going to happen**, were **about to happen**, or were **planned**. Often the plan changed: **iba a tomar el camión, pero me fui caminando**.
Even though it's a past tense, it can refer to something still in the future, a plan you already had: **—¿Vienes al cine? —Es que iba a tomar un café con Beto.**
Don't translate it word for word as **estaba yendo a**: that means you were literally on your way somewhere.
Tip: **iba a** is a plan that left the house but maybe never arrived.

lista.es: ==Iba a tomar== el camión, pero decidí irme caminando.
lista.en: I was going to take the bus, but I decided to walk.

lista.es: Mi hermano ==iba a estudiar== medicina, pero cambió de opinión.
lista.en: My brother was going to study medicine, but he changed his mind.

lista.es: —¿Vienes al cine? —Es que ==iba a tomar== un café con Beto.
lista.en: "Are you coming to the movies?" "Well, I was going to have coffee with Beto."

lista.es: Me tengo que quedar hasta las tres. ¡Qué lástima! ==Iba a llamar== a Beto para ir por tacos.
lista.en: I have to stay until three. What a shame! I was going to call Beto to go for tacos.

lista.es: ==Íbamos a surfear==, pero no hubo olas.
lista.en: We were going to surf, but there were no waves.

lista.texto: The present version: [[7067|ir a for plans]].
**Ir** in the imperfect: [[5269|ir in the imperfect]].

bloques.texto: Say it out loud, then open the answer.

lista.p: In Spanish: _I was going to call you._ (tú)
In Spanish: _We were going to eat at the taquería._
lista.r: Íbamos a comer en la taquería.
